title.english: Greetings and Set Phrases for Everyday Life
title.japanese: {挨|あい}{拶|さつ}と{決|き}まり{文|もん}{句|く}

body:
## Phrases with a Time and a Place

Japanese daily life runs on ⟦{挨拶|あいさつ}→挨拶：02505_aisatsu⟧ (greetings) and ⟦{決|き}まり{文句|もんく}→決まり文句：21431_kimarimonku⟧ (set phrases). They are said at fixed moments — leaving the house, sitting down to eat, arriving at a friend's door, finishing work — and most of them have no exact English equivalent, because English does not mark those moments at all. Learning them is less a matter of vocabulary than of knowing **when** to say them. Many come in a casual and a polite version, and choosing the right one is part of using the phrase correctly.

## Through the Day

- ⟦おはよう→おはよう：05205_ohayou⟧ / ⟦おはようございます→おはようございます：30844_ohayougozaimasu⟧ — Good morning. Used until about ten or eleven; in many workplaces it is also the first greeting of the day whenever your shift starts, even in the evening.
- ⟦こんにちは→こんにちは：02839_konnichiha⟧ — Hello, good afternoon. Not used among family or close colleagues you see every day.
- ⟦こんばんは→こんばんは：27858_konbanha⟧ — Good evening.
- ⟦おやすみ→おやすみ：05206_oyasumi⟧ / ⟦おやすみなさい→おやすみなさい：16581_oyasuminasai⟧ — Good night, said when someone is going to bed or when parting late at night.

## Leaving and Coming Home

These four phrases are exchanged in pairs and are used every single day in Japanese households, offices, and schools.

- ⟦{行|い}ってきます→行ってきます：01029_ittekimasu⟧ — I'm off (literally "I'll go and come back"), said by the person leaving.
- ⟦{行|い}っ→行く：00119_iku⟧てらっしゃい — See you later, take care, said by the person staying.
- ⟦ただいま→ただいま：01062_tadaima⟧ — I'm home (literally "just now"), said on returning.
- ⟦おかえり→おかえり：09380_okaeri⟧ / ⟦お{帰|かえ}りなさい→お帰りなさい：01042_okaerinasai⟧ — Welcome back, the reply.

## Meals

- ⟦いただきます→いただきます：00946_itadakimasu⟧ — said before eating, with the hands together. Literally "I humbly receive," it thanks the cook, the host, and the food itself. Say it even when eating alone.
- ⟦ごちそうさま→ごちそうさま：00929_gochisousama⟧ / ⟦ごちそうさまでした→ごちそうさまでした：30845_gochisousamadeshita⟧ — said after eating, and also to a host or a restaurant staff member on leaving; literally "it was a feast."

## Visiting and Being Visited

- ⟦お{邪魔|じゃま}します→お邪魔します：23567_ojamashimasu⟧ — said when stepping into someone's home ("excuse me for intruding"); ⟦お{邪魔|じゃま}しました→お邪魔しました：23568_ojamashimashita⟧ when leaving.
- ⟦いらっしゃい→いらっしゃい：01912_irasshai⟧ — Welcome, come in. Shops and restaurants use the more formal ⟦いらっしゃいませ→いらっしゃいませ：18829_irasshaimase⟧.
- ⟦どうぞ→どうぞ：02920_douzo⟧ — Please, go ahead: offered with a seat, a cup of tea, or an open door.
- ⟦{失礼|しつれい}します→失礼します：21922_shitsureishimasu⟧ — Excuse me, said on entering or leaving an office or a room; the past form ⟦{失礼|しつれい}しました→失礼する：15203_shitsureisuru⟧ apologizes for something you have just done.

## At Work

- ⟦お{疲|つか}れ{様|さま}→お疲れ様：05208_otsukaresama⟧ / お{疲|つか}れさまです / ⟦お{疲|つか}れ{様|さま}→お疲れ様：05208_otsukaresama⟧でした — the all-purpose workplace phrase: a greeting to colleagues, thanks for effort, and a goodbye at the end of the day. Use です to someone still working and でした to someone finishing.
- ⟦ご{苦労|くろう}{様|さま}→ご苦労様：18374_gokurousama⟧ — thanks for your work, said only downward, from a superior to a subordinate. Never say it to your boss.
- ⟦お{先|さき}に→お先に：26563_osakini⟧⟦{失礼|しつれい}します→失礼します：21922_shitsureishimasu⟧ — Excuse me for leaving before you, said when going home while others are still working. The usual reply is ⟦お{疲|つか}れ{様|さま}→お疲れ様：05208_otsukaresama⟧でした.
- ⟦お{世話|せわ}になっております→お世話になっております：23569_osewaninatteorimasu⟧ — a standard opening on the phone and in email to clients and business partners ("thank you for your continued support"); ⟦お{世話|せわ}になりました→お世話になりました：30848_osewaninarimashita⟧ when a relationship or a stay ends.
- ⟦よろしくお{願|ねが}いします→よろしくお願いします：23566_yoroshikuonegaishimasu⟧ — the phrase that closes introductions, requests, and emails. It asks for goodwill in the relationship to come, and has no English equivalent; "I look forward to working with you" comes closest.

## Meeting People

- ⟦はじめまして→初めまして：00934_hajimemashite⟧ — How do you do, on first meeting, followed by your name and ⟦よろしくお{願|ねが}いします→よろしくお願いします：23566_yoroshikuonegaishimasu⟧.
- ⟦{久|ひさ}しぶり→久しぶり：01711_hisashiburi⟧ / お⟦{久|ひさ}しぶり→久しぶり：01711_hisashiburi⟧です — Long time no see. The very formal version, ⟦ご{無沙汰|ぶさた}→ご無沙汰：10326_gobusata⟧⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧おります, apologizes for not having been in touch.
- お⟦{元気|げんき}→元気：00696_genki⟧です⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧ — How are you? Unlike English "how are you," this is asked only after some time apart, and the standard answer is ⟦おかげさまで→おかげさまで：26572_okagesamade⟧ ("thanks to you"), which can also stand alone as a modest "I'm fine."

## Thanks and Apologies

- ⟦ありがとう→ありがとう：00917_arigatou⟧ / ⟦ありがとうございます→ありがとうございます：09886_arigatougozaimasu⟧ / ⟦ありがとうございました→ありがとうございました：30846_arigatougozaimashita⟧ — Thank you; the past form is used once the favor is complete.
- ⟦どういたしまして→どういたしまして：05207_douitashimashite⟧ — You're welcome, though a modest ⟦いいえ→いいえ：02845_iie⟧ or ⟦とんでもない→とんでもない：03470_tondemonai⟧ is more common.
- ⟦すみません→すみません：00998_sumimasen⟧ — Excuse me, sorry, and thank you all at once: it apologizes, gets attention, and acknowledges a favor that cost someone effort.
- ⟦ごめん→御免：00072_gomen⟧ / ⟦ごめんなさい→ごめんなさい：00931_gomennasai⟧ — Sorry, for personal apologies among people you know.
- ⟦{申|もう}し{訳|わけ}ありません→申し訳ありません：21409_moushiwakearimasen⟧ / ⟦{申|もう}し{訳|わけ}ございません→申し訳ございません：18087_moushiwakegozaimasen⟧ — I am very sorry, the formal apology used in business and to customers.
- ⟦お{待|ま}たせ→お待たせ：27262_omatase⟧⟦しました→する：00392_suru⟧ — Sorry to have kept you waiting; heard at every counter and restaurant.
- ⟦{恐|おそ}れ{入|い}ります→恐れ入る：05914_osoreiru⟧ — a formal thank-you or apology for troubling someone, used when asking a favor or accepting help.
- ⟦こちらこそ→こちらこそ：30849_kochirakoso⟧ — The pleasure is mine; likewise. The reply when someone thanks you or says ⟦よろしくお{願|ねが}いします→よろしくお願いします：23566_yoroshikuonegaishimasu⟧ and you feel the same.

## Special Occasions

- ⟦おめでとう→おめでとう：01043_omedetou⟧ / ⟦おめでとうございます→おめでとうございます：30847_omedetougozaimasu⟧ — Congratulations, for birthdays, weddings, exams passed, and new babies.
- ⟦お{大事|だいじ}に→お大事に：26564_odaijini⟧ — Take care of yourself, to someone who is ill.
- ⟦{気|き}をつけて→気をつけて：01080_kiwotsukete⟧ — Take care, be careful, said to someone setting out on a trip or heading home.
- ⟦{頑張|がんば}って→頑張る：01222_ganbaru⟧ — Good luck, do your best, before an exam, a match, or a hard day.
- ⟦ようこそ→ようこそ：27879_youkoso⟧ — Welcome, to a visitor or a new member.
- ⟦{明|あ}けましておめでとうございます→明けましておめでとうございます：30851_akemashiteomedetougozaimasu⟧ — Happy New Year, said from January 1 onward and followed by ⟦{今年|ことし}→今年：00722_kotoshi⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦よろしくお{願|ねが}いします→よろしくお願いします：23566_yoroshikuonegaishimasu⟧; before the year ends, people part with ⟦{良|よ}いお{年|とし}を→良いお年を：30852_yoiotoshiwo⟧ (have a good New Year).

## Tips for Learners

1. **Learn the pairs together.** ⟦{行|い}ってきます→行ってきます：01029_ittekimasu⟧ expects ⟦{行|い}っ→行く：00119_iku⟧てらっしゃい; ⟦ただいま→ただいま：01062_tadaima⟧ expects ⟦おかえり→おかえり：09380_okaeri⟧. Half a pair sounds incomplete.
2. **Match the level.** ⟦ございます→ございます：01300_gozaimasu⟧, ⟦なさい→なさる：01307_nasaru⟧, and でした turn a casual phrase into a polite one; use the polite forms with anyone who is not family or a close friend.
3. **Watch the direction.** ⟦ご{苦労|くろう}{様|さま}→ご苦労様：18374_gokurousama⟧ goes only downward; ⟦お{疲|つか}れ{様|さま}→お疲れ様：05208_otsukaresama⟧ works in every direction.
4. **Do not translate ⟦よろしくお{願|ねが}いします→よろしくお願いします：23566_yoroshikuonegaishimasu⟧.** Learn the situations instead: after introductions, when asking a favor, at the end of a request.
5. **Use ⟦すみません→すみません：00998_sumimasen⟧ generously.** It is the most versatile phrase in the language, and it is rarely wrong.
6. **See also** [The Basic Keigo System](keigo.html) for the polite forms these phrases are built on, and [Referring to People](referring-to-people.html) for how to address the people you greet.
